goal: Our firewall shows a workstation connecting to 162.243.103.246 on port 8080 a few times last night. Is this C2 traffic and what should I do?

plan.understanding: The analyst wants to determine if outbound connections from a workstation to IP 162.243.103.246 on port 8080 represent Command and Control (C2) traffic and what remediation steps to take.
assumptions: The IP address 162.243.103.246 is public and can be queried via external threat intelligence tools.
"Last night" refers to the evening of 2026-11-18.
plan.done_when: The investigation results from threat intel, internet DB, registration, and web search are synthesized to provide a verdict on whether the IP is malicious/C2, along with actionable recommendations for the analyst.

steps.why: Check AlienVault OTX for known malicious pulses, tags, and associated malware families.
Query Shodan InternetDB for open ports, hostnames, and explicit tags like C2 or VPN.
Retrieve ownership and registration details to see if it belongs to a known hosting provider or legitimate service.
Verify if the IP is currently operating as a Tor exit node.
Perform a broader web search to find any public mentions, abuse reports, or threat intel write-ups regarding this IP.

result.summary: An analysis of the external IP address 162.243.103.246 showed historical associations with malware botnet Command and Control infrastructure, specifically Feodo Tracker / Emotet C&C indicators, alongside open ports including 8080. The IP is hosted on DigitalOcean cloud infrastructure with associated hostnames such as wearoddball.com.

findings.text: InternetDB lookup shows the IP 162.243.103.246 is active on ports 22, 80, 443, and 8080, and is hosted on cloud infrastructure with associated hostnames 'www.wearoddball.com' and 'wearoddball.com'.
RDAP lookup confirms the IP belongs to DigitalOcean, LLC and was registered in September 2013.
Tor exit node check confirms the IP is not a Tor exit node.
Web search results tie the IP address to AbuseIPDB and Feodo Tracker referencing historical Emotet C&C activity.

recommendations: Isolate the workstation that initiated outbound connections to IP 162.243.103.246 on port 8080.
Perform a forensic triage and malware scan on the affected workstation to check for potential Emotet or other botnet infections.
Block outbound traffic to IP 162.243.103.246 at the firewall level if unauthorized.
gaps: AlienVault OTX lookup failed due to a timeout error.
Initial targeted web search for the specific IP string yielded no results due to query syntax issues.
